summary: 61-year-old woman with stage IV ovarian cancer and carcinomatosis, 4 days of vomiting and distension; CT: multiple transition points, ascites. Goals: comfort and home.

inputs.hpi: Stage IV ovarian cancer with peritoneal disease, on third-line chemotherapy. 4 days of intermittent colicky pain, vomiting after every meal, increasing distension, small amounts of flatus. Lost 6 kg in 2 months. Her goals: to be comfortable and to go home; she does not want a big operation.

exam.abdomen: Distended with shifting dullness; multiple firm peritoneal nodules; mild diffuse tenderness, no peritonism.

imaging.name: CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast
imaging.result: Small bowel obstruction with multiple transition points related to peritoneal carcinomatosis; moderate ascites. No perforation, no closed loop.

comorbidities: Ovarian cancer — stage IV, peritoneal carcinomatosis

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Malignant small bowel obstruction
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Malignant small bowel obstruction from peritoneal carcinomatosis (multiple transition points) — palliative, symptom-focused management with oncology and palliative care.

socratesAnswers.associated: Vomiting after meals, distension, weight loss

mustInclude.note: Individualised decision with oncology/palliative care and the patient's goals.
mustInclude.knownGapNote: Web: No palliative, oncology or goals-of-care step for malignant obstruction; the plan is the generic bowel-obstruction protocol.
mustInclude.proposedFix: Add a malignant-SBO variant (carcinomatosis, multiple transition points) with palliative/oncology MDT and MASCC medical management.

mustInclude.note: MASCC 2021: antisecretory, antiemetic and corticosteroid options; venting gastrostomy.
mustInclude.knownGapNote: Web: No antisecretory/antiemetic/steroid or venting-gastrostomy option.

mustExclude.note: Multiple transition points with carcinomatosis: surgery is rarely beneficial; not a default operative plan.

guideline.name: WSES Bologna guidelines — adhesive small bowel obstruction (2017 update)
guideline.section: CT with IV contrast for strangulation signs; non-operative management (NGT, fluids) up to 72 h without strangulation; water-soluble contrast challenge (colon within 24 h predicts success); surgery for strangulation, peritonitis or failed NOM; virgin abdomen and hernia causes
guideline.citation: ten Broek RPG, Krielen P, Di Saverio S, et al. Bologna guidelines for diagnosis and management of adhesive small bowel obstruction (ASBO): 2017 update of the evidence-based guidelines from the WSES ASBO working group. World J Emerg Surg. 2018;13:24.

guideline.name: MASCC guidelines — malignant bowel obstruction
guideline.section: Individualised, palliative-focused decision-making; medical management (antisecretory, antiemetic); venting gastrostomy; selective surgery
guideline.citation: Davis M, Hui D, Davies A, et al. Medical management of malignant bowel obstruction in patients with advanced cancer: 2021 MASCC guideline update. Support Care Cancer. 2021;29:8089–96.

rationale: Permutation: malignant obstruction. Outside the adhesive-SBO algorithm: the plan should be individualised and palliative-focused (MASCC 2021), not a default drip-and-suck or emergency laparotomy template.
